correctness.rationale: A self-contained proof diagonalizes the Gaussian radial localization form in the normalized monomial basis, computes adjacent differences exactly as a nonzero exponential polynomial, proves its at-most-2K-1 real-zero bound by Rolle induction, and converts variation to an at-most-K strict-peak bound including boundary index 0. A separated-ring induction establishes sharpness simultaneously for every positive K; its key comparisons are derived from explicit expansions with nonzero 1/(8M) and -3/(8M) coefficients, versus the old-band O(B^(M+1)) tail. The finite checker separately illustrates K=1..4 and 32 exact identity comparisons numerically; it is not relied upon as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2025 finite-annulus work supplies unordered eigenvalues and their rearranged large-scale profile, not this natural-degree exact modal cap with attainment for every K. Knutsen 2020 gives the single-ring case and Daubechies 1988 the radial formula. Yu 2011 and Karlin supply classical variation-diminishing machinery, which is acknowledged as prior coverage of the upper-bound mechanism. The sharp K-band unweighted realization has not been located as an asserted or demonstrably implied published result under inspected statements. Implicit earlier coverage remains a real originality risk.
residual_risks: Karlin 1968 book not inspected directly: sufficiently general sharpness consequences of strict total positivity might imply the separated-band realization.
An unindexed Poisson-mixture or time-frequency localization theorem could already state this exact K-band sharp multimodality classification.
The 2012 inverse-problem preprint was compared by abstract, not full body; although its stated simply connected converse is inapplicable, unseen material could be relevant.

value.rationale: For radial Gaussian localization, band topology forces a sharp universal maximum of K strict natural Hermite eigenvalue peaks and 2K-1 spectral sign changes. This is a complete quantitative modal-complexity cap for all component counts and all real endpoints, with matching examples for every K; it distinguishes modal order from trivially monotone sorted spectral order. Structural insight about disconnected observation geometry motivates the invariant independently of computations; neither a chosen numeric slice nor the classical zero lemma alone expresses the full sharp spectral result.
